findings: The loaded profile contains only VLESS TCP; the recent HY2 UDP-buffer and HY2 BBR changes are not applied to this client transport. This is a concrete client configuration gap, not proof that WAN caused the Fast regression.

Netflix API and nflxvideo transfer hosts match Netflix -> STATIC-SELECT before China-IP and default rules. Custom Direct and other cached domain/inline providers did not match the tested public hostnames.

fast.com/api.fast.com had no hostname-specific match in current cached providers; default is STATIC-SELECT, but earlier IP rules must be checked against actual connection destination to prove frontend direction.
Current server evidence excludes a configured 5 Mbps account cap or installed tc policer/class cap.
Old standalone and current generated HY2 use ignoreClientBandwidth=true and BBRstandard; new generated nodes have no up/down bandwidth fields.
The only retained recent runtime setting is a larger UDP socket ceiling. The apply lifecycle preserves qdisc semantics and Xray epochs. BBR trial runtime was restored byte-for-byte.

The older architecture used HY2 direct outbounds; multiuser uses authenticated loopback SOCKS/Xray AUTO. This is a real historical change to test if an updated HY2 client still underperforms, but it is not the loaded VLESS route.

Short single-stream Cloudflare measurements cannot reproduce or disprove a historical multi-stream Fast Netflix result; compare the same signed Fast target and same number of streams with forced TCP and HY2.
limits: Hostname audit is not an observation of actual Fast connections; DNS-selected IP and client runtime chain remain necessary.
Existing reports do not reproduce the user historical 200 Mbps Fast result.
The sample nflxvideo hostname tests suffix rules, not the precise signed target currently selected by Fast.
Current idle CPU and UDP counters do not establish load capacity.
